hypothesis_card.mechanism: AWS reprices spot per instance family in multi-month waves (price-list churn is continuous: CostPulse 2024-08-02 shows 65,388 cuts vs 259,823 increases in one EC2 publication). A family whose median level rose over the trailing 90 days is in an up-wave; over the next 90-180 days its administered moves keep skewing up, so the pooled 730-day change quantiles (which average over up- and down-waves) under-cover the upper tail exactly there. Adding k*clip(famtr,0,0.4)*(h/180) to q90 only (h>=90) prices that skew; the q10 side stays byte-identical because falling families breach q10 and widening it was measured loss-negative (-0.002/-0.004).
hypothesis_card.expected_observation: Discovery pooled 0.2675 -> ~0.277 (+0.009), h90 +0.017 / h180 +0.006, q90 breach 24.6% -> ~20.6%, coverage +0.024, 12/16 origins improved; dense stride-14 backtest pooled delta ~+0.010 with ~85% of origins improved. On Holdout: pooled ~0.295-0.300 vs gate-1 threshold 0.2916, coverage ~0.78 (in band), all horizons positive.
hypothesis_card.competing_explanation: The rival explanation of the same errors: the q90 breaches are not trend-persistence but a generic under-dispersion of the 730-day pooled change quantiles at h90/h180 (any unconditional widening would fix them), and the gain is a width-for-skill trade that will not transfer. Evidence against: unconditional/symmetric widening was measured loss-negative in this lab's prior stages and the down-side (q10) widening tested here is negative (-0.002/-0.004 h90/h180) while the up-side is positive — a generic under-dispersion story would reward both sides; the gain also concentrates exactly where the trend signal is largest (rising p5 families, coverage 0.52-0.67 -> 0.57-0.69).
hypothesis_card.test: Pseudo-origin scan (12 monthly pods 2023-07..2024-06, point-in-time): up-side widening k=0.5/1.0 monotone positive (h90 0.322->0.331->0.337, h180 0.363->0.366->0.369), down-side negative; then dry run on the 16 scored Discovery origins (pooled 0.2766 vs champion 0.2675, +0.0091, h90 +0.0174, h180 +0.0059, coverage 0.664->0.688, q90 breach 24.6%->20.6%, 12/16 origins, screen PASS) and a dense stride-14 backtest over 33 origins (pooled delta +0.0101, 85% of origins improved, h90 +0.0179 / h180 +0.0075).
hypothesis_card.rejection_condition: Rejected if Discovery pooled <= 0.2675 (measured 0.2766, screen PASS) or sanity fails. The trend-widening mechanism is falsified if the holdout pooled gain over the champion (0.2886) is below +0.003 (gate 1), or if holdout coverage_80 leaves [0.74, 0.86] (gate 3) — i.e. the widening bought width without coverage. The direction claim is falsified if the h90 gain specifically fails to transfer (holdout h90 <= 0.2226, the champion's value).

hypothesis: Family-trend-scaled q90 widening (regime_change): the h90/h180 q90 breaches concentrate in instance families whose spot level has been RISING over the last 90 days (p5 coverage 0.52-0.67 vs falling p4d breaching q10), because AWS's administered repricing continues in the trend direction at long horizons; widening ONLY the upper quantile of rising families by k*clip(family 90d trend, 0, 0.4)*(h/180) with k=1.0 (q10 byte-identical, down-side measured loss-negative) cuts the 16-32% q90 breach loss. Stacked on the per-series x family change-quantile blend (w=0.3 at h90, 0.5 at h180, >=30 own pairs else family fallback) from the same diagnosis.
market_insight: The forecast assumes AWS GPU spot prices at 30-180-day horizons are administered in family-level repricing waves whose direction persists for quarters: a family whose cross-sectional level rose over the last 90 days (p5/H100 premium capacity through 2023-24 AI demand; NextPlatform 2024-05-02 H100 allocation data, TechSpot 2024-02-27 easing H100 lead times) keeps repricing upward, so its q90 must be widened by the recent family trend, while falling families (p4d/A100, repriced down as Capacity Blocks reclaim idle capacity — AWS News Blog 2023-10-31 aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/announcing-amazon-ec2-capacity-blocks-for-ml; re:Invent 2024 capacity-management recap, zenn.dev/articles/831696491092b17) breach q10, not q90, and their lower band is left untouched. Dated evidence that AWS reprices continuously rather than drifting freely: the 2024-08-02 EC2 price-list publication churn (costpulse.io/aws-price-changes/amazon-elastic-compute-cloud/20240802172840: 65,388 cuts vs 259,823 increases in one version) — direction-mixed at instance level, which is exactly why the lever uses the pack's own family trend rather than news. The view would change if family trends mean-reverted within 90 days (then the widening buys width without coverage), if a generation transition (p6/Blackwell) repriced p5 down monotonically (the up-only widening would over-cover), or if the Holdout coverage left the [0.74, 0.86] band.
bottleneck: Data. (1) 116/133 target series have no history at Discovery origins, so family cross-sections are thin (12-17 series) and per-series levers cannot be validated for the p5e/p6 families that dominate Holdout; (2) exogenous news remains direction-mixed (4th falsification: the only quantitative feed found, CostPulse 2024-08-02, is RHEL repricing, not GPU spot); (3) 2 of 6 analyses were spent debugging a truth-lookup bug in the pseudo-origin harness (history must be taken from the full slice, not truncated at the pod) — the fixed harness is reusable next episode.
